d:chapter.d:title: Pair of Straight Lines
d:chapter.d:para: Consider a pair of straight lines $ax + by + c = 0$ and $a_1x + b_1y + c_1 = 0$, which we represent as $(ax + by + c)(a_1x + b_1y + c_1) = 0$.
Let $P(\alpha, beta)$ on the line $ax + by + c = 0 \Rightarrow a\alpha + b\beta + c = 0$ and $(a\alpha + b\beta + c)$$(a_1\alpha + b_1\beta + c_1) = 0$.
Thus, a point which lies on either line wil satisfy $(ax + by + c)(a_1x + b_1y + c_1) = 0$. This equation represents a pair of straight lines.

d:sect1.d:title: Homogeneous Equations
d:sect1.d:para: Any equation in which combined powers of $x$ and $y$ is constant(say $n$) is called a homogeneous equation of degree $n$. For example, $ax^22 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$ is a homogeneous equation of degree $2$.

d:sect1.d:title: Pair of Straight Lines Through Origin
d:sect1.d:para: We will show that any homogeneous equation of second degree in $x$ and $y$ represents a pair of straight lines through the origin.
Consider the equation $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0 \Rightarrow a + b\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)62 + 2h\frac{y}{x} = 0$, which is a quadratic equation in $\frac{y}{x}$.
Let the roots be $m_1$ and $m_2$ of the above equation. $\Rightarrow \frac{y}{x} = m_1, m_2\Rightarrow b(y - m_1x)(y - m_2x) = 0.$
Thus, the given homogeneous equation represents two straight lines through origin.
If the lines are represented by $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$ and $y - m_1x = 0$ and $y - m_2x = 0$, then

d:sect1.d:title: Angle Between the Lines Represented by Second Degree Equation
d:sect1.d:para: The tangent of the angle between the two lines is given by $\tan\theta = \pm\frac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1m_2} = \pm\frac{\sqrt{\left(m_1 + m_2\right)^2 - 4m_1m_2}}{1 + m_1m_2} = \pm\frac{2\sqrt{h^2 - ab}}{a + b}$
For lines to be perpendicular \[a + b = 0\tag{4.3}\] and for them to be paralle \[h^2 = ab\tag{4.4}\]

d:sect1.d:title: Bisectors of Angles Between the Pair of Straight Lines
d:sect1.d:para: Coninuing from previous sections the equation of bisectors of straight lines is given by $\frac{y - m_1x}{\sqrt{1 + m_1^2}} = \pm\frac{y - m_2x}{\sqrt{1 + m_2^2}}$

Combined equation is given by $\left(\frac{y - m_1x}{\sqrt{1 + m_1^2}} - \frac{y - m_2x}{\sqrt{1 + m_2^2}}\right)\left(\frac{y - m_1x}{\sqrt{1 + m_1^2}} + \frac{y - m_2x}{\sqrt{1 + m_2^2}}\right) = 0$

d:para.m: $\Rightarrow \frac{(y - m_1x)^2}{\sqrt{\left(1 + m_1^2\right)}} - \frac{(y - m_2x)^2}{\left(1 + m_2^2\right)} = (m_1 + m_2)(x^2 - y^2) + 2(m_1m_2 - 1)xy = 0$

d:sect1.d:title: Condition for General Equation of Second Degree to Represent a Pair of Straight Lines
d:sect1.d:para: General equation of the second degree is given by $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$. This equation will result into two straight lines if it can be resolved into two linear factors.
Let the straight lines be $l_1x + m_1y + n_1 = 0$ and $l_2x + m_2y + n_2 = 0$, which are represented by the above equation.
Then $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = (l_1x + m_1y + n_1)(l_2x + m_2y + n_2)$
Comparing coefficients $l_1l_2 = a, m_1m_2 = b, n_1n_2 = c, m_1n_2 + m_2n_2 = 2f, n_1l_2 + n_2l_1 = 2g, l_1m_2 + l_2m_1 = 2h$
Multiplying last three we obtain, \[abc + 2fgh - af^2 - bg^2 - ch^2 = 0\] which is the required condition.
The above condition can be represented as \[\begin{vmatrix}a & h & g\\h & b & f\\g & f & c\end{vmatrix} = 0\tag{4.6}\]

The general equation can be treated as an equation in 𝑥 and then discriminat must be a perfect square for it to resolve into linear factors. We will obtain the same condition as above using this method as well.
